About AfroBot

Giving every child the chance to build the future.

The record so farWrite to AfroBot
The foundation

A program of Glappy Foundation

AfroBot is a kids-only youth robotics and AI program of Glappy Foundation, a Texas nonprofit corporation. Glappy Foundation is separate from Glappy Inc. Children take part through a parent or guardian.

Where it began

Africa, then McKinney

The work started in Africa in November 2022 and has run for about 4 years. A pilot in McKinney, Texas, followed in 2024.

We give children with limited access the tools, mentors and confidence to build the future with robotics and AI.AfroBot’s mission
Timeline

Where the work stands

Since 2022

Africa

Programs in Africa began in November 2022.

2024

McKinney

A 2024 pilot of about 30 students in Texas.

2027

Dallas–Fort Worth

Dallas–Fort Worth scales the 2024 pilot to about 15 teams and about 90 students. Other North America regions stay proposed.

April 2028

Proposed

A Dallas championship is proposed, pending partner confirmation.

The record so far

About 5,000 children have been trained through our holiday programs in Africa.

About 3,200 students are actively learning at partner schools in Africa. The partnership has run since June 2023.

Holiday totals: AfroBot records, November 2026. Partner school reach: signed partnership letter, November 2026.

Access for every child

Robotics and AI should not depend on a family’s income or zip code. Team fees stay low, and sponsors and donors cover the rest. Kits and mentors are provided through partner schools. The focus is communities with fewer STEM opportunities in North America and Africa, and girls and boys are equally welcome.
